record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a real weight-edit abliteration smoke run and its refusal and capability outcomes. This tests the practical-removal version, but does not apply the original all-layer, all-position activation-direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The README also describes a layer-diagnostic feature and says one 0.6B run peaked at L21 while ditch edits were visible from L16 through L28. It does not report an outcome from a causal direction-ablation scan. The reported run is explicitly described as a wiring smoke test, not evidence of significant guardrail removal.
record.test_reason: This is a tooling repo that uses abliteration (Heretic/ditch) as an editor and reports only pipeline wiring. The one real run is a 1-trial smoke test on Qwen3-0.6B with 6 target prompts. Its base refusal was 16.7% (1/6), below the repo's own applicability gate of ≥0.5 ('no guardrail to remove'). The authors say it does not show guardrail removal. No result bears on whether V2 holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say the two smoke runs show the GGUF/HF → ditch → export → eval → gate → report chain works. They say the runs do not show significant guardrail removal on 0.6B. Testing this would need 1.7B/4B models, more held-out prompts, and the audit turned on.
record.recipe_differences: The repo is an experiment-pipeline tool combining Heretic and ditch weight editing with evaluation and gates; it does not report the original all-layer, all-position activation projection intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: The layer-diagnostic tool, on one real 0.6B run, found the refusal-direction projection peak at L21. The ditch weight changes were visible from L16 to L28.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Descriptive localisation of the diff-in-means refusal direction across layers. The authors say it is direction-level evidence only, not causal.

record.problems: The reported result is a single-trial smoke run on a 0.6B model with only 6 held-out target and 6 preserve examples. The refusal rate did not decrease, the gate failed, and uncertainty values are not reported. The README says this does not demonstrate significant guardrail removal.
record.rows_left_out: The HF-input smoke run is mentioned but no separate outcome is given. The README's synthetic demo numbers are explicitly not real-model results and were not recorded as findings.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the difference-in-means direction with a refusal outcome. The per-layer diagnostic gives only a peak-layer note, with no reported effect on refusal.
No meaningful abliteration run. Only a 1-trial smoke test on a 0.6B model with low base refusal; the larger 1.7B/4B runs were not reported.
A compass AUC audit (does the edited model still recognise harm) is designed but no result is reported.
Not tested. Qwen3-0.6B has a thinking mode, but this is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges V2' label is removed. The unchanged refusal rate comes from a one-trial wiring test with 1/6 base refusal, which the authors explicitly disclaim. The repo's own gates would mark this experiment 'not applicable'. The synthetic demo numbers are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No reported test of removing or adding the difference-in-means direction across every layer and position, or of its causal effect on refusal.
Only one Qwen3-0.6B GGUF-input smoke run is reported; this does not establish results across released models.
No reported test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test comparing a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No reported test separating harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No reported cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No reported comparison of refusal training methods or training stages.
No reported test on reasoning models.

rows.subject: Qwen3-0.6B
rows.operation_detail: ditch abliteration from GGUF input, with evaluation using the same-source HF directory

conditions.value: 1-trial smoke; 6 held-out target and 6 preserve examples

rows.note: The README says the gate failed because the reduction was insufficient. It identifies this run as a wiring smoke test and cautions that it does not demonstrate significant guardrail removal.
rows.check: Refusal was 16.7% before and 16.7% after, but this cannot show removal. Base refusal is only 1/6, below the repo's own ≥0.5 applicability threshold. It was a single Optuna trial (no real parameter search) on n=6. The authors call it a wiring smoke test, not evidence of removal. Marking it 'absent' overstates what it shows.
